question: Does the 2026 Nagao Foundation northern Palawan field report provide fish records that are identifiable and waterbody-resolved enough for Bangwit's freshwater coverage?

source.title: Report on survey on Palawan, Philippines (30 April 2026)
source.provider: Nagao Natural Environment Foundation; project collaborators include Western Philippines University
source.citation: Nagao Natural Environment Foundation. (2026). Report on survey on Palawan, Philippines (30 April 2026). Project: Fauna and life history of freshwater and estuarine fish of the Philippines: Toward elucidation of the larval dispersal mechanism of diadromous fish along the Kuroshio Current. 7 pp.

limitationsStatedByReport: The survey was short and not comprehensive.
Only one stream was surveyed; the authors propose sampling additional streams in future work.

habitatLeads.name: Lake Manguao
sourceReportedFindings: Boroda genus goby specimens were collected from Lake Manguao and streams in northern Palawan; the report estimates at least two Boroda species but does not identify them to species.
The report says Lake Manguao contains several endemic species and describes two unnamed Barbodes species at different depths.

habitatLeads.habitat: one northern Palawan stream with a series of waterfalls
sourceReportedFindings: The report says numerous Boroda gobies were observed.
The stream name, reach, sampling date per site, taxon list, voucher IDs, and coordinates are not stated.
The report says gobies, halfbeaks, and Phallostethidae were collected.
No species names or precise estuary locality are given; some specimens were intended for a later population-structure study with Luzon and Okinawa samples.

surveyScope.otherSamplingMention: The report also mentions fish-market sampling during the Palawan trip, but supplies no market-specific species table or locality crosswalk in the report reviewed.

namedFishClaim.name: Pterocryptis taytayensis
namedFishClaim.sourceStatement: The report says the rare, endangered catfish endemic to Palawan was found.

surveyScope.relationToWpu2025PpsrAbstract: No relationship between this northern Palawan survey and the separate WPU 2025 Puerto Princesa Subterranean River abstract is stated; they are not merged.

reuseReview.reportLicense: No open license or item-specific reuse terms were identified in the report or project page reviewed.

limits: This is a concise field-trip report rather than a full methods paper or annotated species checklist.
The Lake Manguao Barbodes are identified only to genus; the estimated Boroda species are not named or individually crosswalked to collection sites.
The single unnamed stream and unnamed mangrove estuary do not support precise waterbody geometry or station-level occurrence rows.
Pterocryptis taytayensis is mentioned as found in Palawan without a waterbody, date, specimen ID, or sequence accession in the report.
No sampling-effort details, specimen repository accessions, species-by-site matrix, coordinates, catchability, diet, fishing rules, or safety status were reviewed.
The report's copyright notice does not provide an open license for copying its images or transforming its observations into a public checklist.

followUp.nextAction: Keep the current northern Palawan field work as a high-priority research lead. If public taxon-by-waterbody data or specimen accession records appear, review their identifications, station attribution, and reuse rights; in parallel, continue other named MIMAROPA freshwater surveys.
